ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and beneficial owners against the Samoa Terrorist Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and international PEP databases; enhanced due diligence is required for any person connected with high-risk jurisdictions, PEP status, adverse media or negative sanctions findings; screening results must be certified by the licensed company service provider before incorporation and must be refreshed if any UBO or signatory changes within the pre-incorporation period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour - Companies Registry, International Companies Section
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registry language is English. International Company names may be in English, Samoan or another language, but all non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into Roman characters prior to registration. Samoan diacritical marks are accepted in local-language names, and a certified transliteration is required where the proposed name is not in Roman script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 working days of the rejection notice. The Registrar must issue a written decision within 14 working days of receipt. A further appeal may be made to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 28 days of the Registrar's final refusal. Judicial review of an adverse ministerial decision is available in the Supreme Court of Samoa. Applicants may submit one alternative name in the original clearance application to avoid procedural delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office of a Samoa International Company. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the location of its licensed registered agent. A remote correspondence address may be used only as a secondary business address and must not replace the statutory physical registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual baseline risk of unannounced inspection of the licensed registered agent's premises; direct on-site inspection risk for a compliant air cargo charter broker is assessed as low, below 5% per year, provided that physical office substance and records are maintained in Samoa.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss.7 (Application for Incorporation), s.9 (Memorandum), s.10 (Articles), s.24 (Registered Office), ss.28-30 (Directors and Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association signed by the subscriber and endorsed by the licensed registered agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Authorized capital is typically set at USD 1,000,000 divided into shares of USD 1.00; the subscriber need only pay up an amount sufficient to satisfy the registered agent's escrow/working capital policy, commonly a minimum of one issued share, being USD 1.00, deposited with the licensed registered agent trust account
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (i) the subscriber named in the Memorandum and Articles of Association be and is hereby allotted one ordinary share of USD 1.00 fully paid, with no further paid-up capital required by law; (ii) the registered office in Samoa as indicated on the Registered Office Notice filed with the Registrar of International Companies be and is hereby adopted, and the licensed registered agent be retained; (iii) the individuals named in the consent filings be and are hereby appointed first directors and officers to hold office until the first annual general meeting; (iv) the directors be and are hereby authorized to open bank accounts, execute banking mandates, and complete any filings required to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent and Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa (acting through licensed registered agents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a professional services agreement with a Samoan licensed registered agent. Instruct the agent to submit a name reservation application to the Registrar; the proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing International Company or domestic company. The name must end with a recognized suffix such as 'Limited', 'Corporation', or 'Inc.' and must not suggest a prohibited activity.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Letter of authorization to the registered agent
Identity and address evidence of the ultimate beneficial owner and subscriber
Bank-reference or certificate of incumbency for introducer (if any)
Payment for name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the agent shall, within one business day, file two alternative names in order of preference; a formal sworn declaration may be provided to overcome an objection based on similarity, or the applicant may adopt a non-offending distinctive name. Refusal grounds based on prohibited terms must be cured by renaming.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent; notarization by a Samoan Notary Public where physical execution is adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association reflecting the chosen share capital, authorized capital of USD 1,000,000, registered office clause, and permitted-object clause aligned with ISIC 5229 air cargo charter brokerage. The subscriber shall execute the documents, with each signature page notarized or witnessed by the registered agent in accordance with section 9(3) of the International Companies Act 1987. Electronic execution may be accepted where the registered agent maintains a compliant verification record.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association signed by subscriber
Articles of Association signed by subscriber
Registered office notice naming the licensed agent's address
Consent to act as director and officer forms
Notarized passport copy of each officer/director (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of rejection or requisition, the registered agent shall promptly rectify the discrepancy by amending the defect clause, re-executing the affected signature pages, and resubmitting within two business days; no new incorporation fee is triggered if the amendment is ministerial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Application for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa (filed electronically via the registered agent portal or delivered physically to the Companies Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits Form IC-1, together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered office notice, consents of directors and officers, and payment of the statutory filing fee of USD 250. The Registrar examines the documents for formal compliance. Upon approval, the Registrar enters the International Company into the Register of International Companies and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 application for incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (original)
Registered office notice
Consents to act of each director and officer
Evidence of payment of state filing fee (USD 250)
Copy of registered agent's license and authorization letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the agent shall respond within the statutory 21-day cure period, or such shorter period as the Registrar directs, by provision of the corrected forms or clarification letter. If the application is rejected due to non-compliance, a fresh application may be filed after curing the defect; no new fee applies if rejection is attributable to the Registrar's administrative error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Register Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation. The registered agent shall then prepare the company's statutory registers, including the register of shareholders, register of directors and officers, and minutes of the first board resolution. The company files its first annual return confirmation and establishes its corporate book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by Registrar)
Statutory registers (shareholders, directors, officers, charges)
Minutes of the pro-forma first board resolution
Bank account opening documentation for corporate banking
Registered agent's certificate of good standing (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error, the agent shall return the original certificate with a written request for rectification under the Registrar's administrative correction procedure; a corrected certificate is re-issued within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance and Compliance Calibration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; registered agent as corporate secretary; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for annual return administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or pass a written resolution) to adopt the tax-free status election under the International Companies Act 1987, ratify the registered agent contract, approve the share record, and authorize opening of a banc account. The company is exempt from Samoan income tax on international business income; however, an annual return and annual government fee are due to the Registrar within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation. As an offshore International Company, the entity is prohibited from carrying on domestic business within Samoa except under special exemption.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolutions of the first board meeting
Share register and allotment statements
Annual return form
Payment for annual government license fee
Tax exemption acknowledgment (no tax filing required for IC)
Compliance policy statement addressing AML for air cargo charter brokerage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is late-filed, the company may apply for reinstatement or relief of late penalties by demonstrating reasonable cause; where the company has inadvertently engaged in domestic business, a curative deregistration of the offending conduct and a written undertaking to the Registrar shall be submitted without delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA) and Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI), licensing division for air freight operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Air Cargo Charter Broker Licence (Freight Forwarding and Charter Booking Licence) issued under the Civil Aviation Act 2008 and the Civil Aviation (Air Services Licensing) Regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa – Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA Registration/Limited Assessment since the air cargo charter broker functions as a non-asset-based intermediary; a full Environmental Impact Assessment will only be required if the entity constructs cargo handling premises, warehousing, or aircraft maintenance facilities in Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Waste Management Regulations 2016 for any fuel or cargo residue; wastewater discharge limits at BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L and suspended solids ≤ 50 mg/L for any future ground handling facility; VOC and hazardous air emissions must meet the MNRE ambient air quality guidelines where cargo fumigation or cold-chain propellant activities occur; transboundary movement of ozone-depleting substances is prohibited.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for any leased office or warehousing footprint; structural load certification from the Samoa National Building Code 2022 and MWTI for any physical installation; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational and Environmental Health Act 2006, including crane/lifting equipment inspection for any cargo handling operations; the entity must also obtain a business premise clearance from the Apia Urban Development Division where a physical office is maintained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa; online taxpayer portal: https://www.mfr.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) obtains a Samoa Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) by submitting to the MfR: (i) certified certificate of incorporation issued under the International Companies Act 1987; (ii) registered office confirmation; (iii) notarized passport copies of all directors and shareholders; (iv) completed TIN application form; and (v) proof of appointment of the licensed registered agent. The MfR issues the TIN within 5-10 business days; the IC then files annual returns with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Registry through the licensed agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists. The International Companies Act 1987 grants an automatic statutory exemption from Samoan income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty and VAGST on international business income; an IC may elect to redomicile or convert to a domestic company, thereby entering the standard resident tax net, but such election is irrevocable for one tax year.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover (VAGST Act 2003); ICs making exclusively international supplies and holding exempt status are not required to register unless they make local taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API clearance is yet mandatory in Samoa; taxpayers file VAGST returns electronically through the MfR e-services portal, and invoices may be issued in paper or electronic form subject to retention for at least 7 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered person may apply the 0% rate to: (i) goods exported from Samoa outside any free zone; and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply, where the direct benefit is consumed outside Samoa. Air cargo charter brokerage fees for international legs qualify where the principal contract evidences a foreign destination and the broker retains shipping documents.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Samoa permits VAGST refunds within 45 days of application; fraudulent zero-rating or false export documentation attracts penalties under the VAGST Act 2003 of up to WST 100,000 fine and/or up to 7 years imprisonment, plus reassessment clawback for up to 8 years from the year of assessment, with interest at the statutory rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Falefa), acting jointly with the Minister of Finance as the exchange control authority under the Exchange Control Act 1971 (as amended), and as the AML/CFT supervisor under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is partially convertible. Current-account flows such as freight payments, commissions and insurance are liberally approved through CBS-licensed authorized dealers, but capital-account transactions including equity injections, intragroup debt and external transfers exceeding WST 200,000 equivalent must either obtain CBS exchange control approval or rely on a statutory exemption. International Companies incorporated under the International Companies Act 2012 are exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1971 in respect of their foreign-currency, non-resident offshore business; the air-cargo charter brokerage can accordingly hold USD brokerage commissions offshore or in a licensed USD account in Samoa without profit-remittance restriction or Samoan withholding tax. Any WST conversion or payment to a Samoan resident, however, still passes through an authorized dealer and remains monitorable by the Central Bank of Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Samoan resident exporters, the Exchange Control Act 1971 and CBS administrative directives impose mandatory repatriation and 100% surrender of export proceeds into WST through an authorized dealer within three (3) months of export entitlement or receipt, unless a specific CBS retention or exemption approval is granted. The air-cargo charter-broker IC is treated as a non-resident under the International Companies Act 2012, so USD charter commissions and disbursement recoveries are not export proceeds subject to the surrender rule and may be retained in a designated USD account. To preserve this treatment, the IC must not book Samoan-source invoicing through a resident branch or permanent establishment, and the licensed Samoan registered agent must maintain the IC records exclusively in the offshore exempt segment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Account (primary clearing) and WST Capital Escrow Account (capital injection retention)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Samoa Holdings Limited (National Bank of Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Foreign-Currency Account and WST Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary clearing rail; Medium only as a supplementary offshore USD collection vehicle. Samoa has no fintech EMI licensing category, and the Exchange Control Act 1971 channels resident payment business through CBS-authorized dealers. Practical legal constraints: (1) Samoan banks generally reject inbound MT103 transfers from unregulated digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business or Currenxie due to source-of-funds opacity and correspondent de-risking; (2) the EMI nostro chain is fragile for USD clearing; and (3) a CBS review will not accept an EMI as evidence of regulated banking status. If used, the EMI must provide per-transaction beneficiary and purpose data and the IC must periodically sweep balances into the primary Samoan USD account by SWIFT MT103.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: On-site in-person identity verification is effectively mandatory for at least one director, the company secretary, or a board-appointed representative holding a notarized power of attorney endorsed by the IC's licensed Samoan registered agent. Remote video KYC is accepted only for low-risk pre-existing clients and should not be assumed for a new International Company air-cargo charter broker. Required pre-interview bundle: Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent certificate, register of directors and shareholders, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, charter-broker trade reference, management or audited accounts, sanctions-screening clearance, and certified passports of all signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual in-and-out liquidity pattern with high-velocity onward payments to third-party aircraft operators and block-space providers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed charter brokerage agreements with commission structure; GSA and block-space agreements; airline operator invoices and settlement schedules; aircraft registration, air operator certificate and hull/liability insurance certificates; and a transactional narrative mapping each inbound commission to a specific outbound disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity where the IC is held by a Samoan or foreign trust, foundation, or nominee chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent attestation under the International Companies Act 2012; trust deed or foundation charter; ultimate beneficial owner declaration; apostilled notarial extracts; chain-of-title share certificates; and CBS/FIU-compliant source-of-wealth statements for each natural-person principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and denied-party exposure in air cargo routing, including transit or counterparties in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC, EU, UN and national consolidated sanctions screening logs covering counterparties, banks, aircraft operators and cargo end-users; denied-party screening results retained for five years; geographic routing restrictions coded into the brokerage policy; and contractual OFAC/UN embargo clauses in every charter agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction and purpose-code mismatch on SWIFT MT103 messages, including generic trade narratives concealing charter disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBPR+ compliant MT103 with precise purpose codes for aircraft charter hire, air freight commission and aviation insurance; aligned commercial invoice and payment instruction file; CBS balance-of-payments reporting code confirmation from the authorized dealer; and documented reconciliation of each transfer to the underlying charter event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction payment red flags such as UAE free zones, Nigeria, Hong Kong shell payables, or payments to personal accounts of pilots or aircraft owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file with corporate ownership, license and sanctions clearance for each high-risk payee; prohibition of personal-account disbursement in the treasury mandate; second-level sign-off by the licensed registered agent; and invoice plus proof of service including air waybill, log, landing and overflight confirmation before release.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank directly to the IC's USD account at the Samoan authorized dealer, with a memo line stating 'Capital injection - International Companies Act 2012 exchange-control exempt' and the ISIC 5229 air-cargo charter brokerage purpose. Pre-funding verification requires: (i) board resolution allotting shares; (ii) updated share register and register of directors; (iii) registered agent certificate; (iv) CBS exchange-control declaration notification where the aggregate injection exceeds WST 200,000 equivalent; (v) three-month bank statements and source-of-funds declaration from the subscribing shareholder; and (vi) certified directors' and signatories' passports and powers of attorney. Samoa does not use IBAN; beneficiary identification is the bank's SWIFT BIC plus the IC's USD account number, and the receiving bank must reject the inbound MT103 if the narrative lacks the purpose code or references a mismatched beneficiary legal name. Equity proceeds may be held in USD without CBS surrender until deployed for charter disbursements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements covering charter hire, block-space prepayments, aviation fuel, overflight and landing fees, insurance premiums and brokerage commissions are cleared via SWIFT MT103 against the bank's USD nostro in New York, with Fedwire or CHIPS used for same-day USD value where the beneficiary bank requires it. Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) are used for material prepayments typically above USD 100,000 equivalent under ACMI and block-space agreements; the documentary set comprises the signed charter agreement, air waybill or GSA acceptance, airline invoice, insurance certificate, and aircraft registration or air operator certificate extract. All outbound disbursements are matched to an underlying charter event, pass a senior compliance sign-off, and are reported to the Central Bank of Samoa through the authorized dealer's monthly balance-of-payments return. Payments to Samoan resident parties require WST conversion through the authorized dealer; payments to non-resident parties are executed in USD and are free of Samoan withholding tax under the International Companies Act 2012.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/WST FX forwards executed with a CBS-licensed authorized dealer, tenor limited to 12 months and supported by documented charter receivables or payables exposure.

Offshore USD/WST non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only where an onshore deliverable forward market is absent and the hedge is supported by a signed charter contract or firm commitment, with the swap confirmation retained for CBS and FIU audit.
USD/WST cross-currency swaps used to hedge long-term block-space, aircraft lease-in or capital commitment exposures, subject to authorized-dealer credit approval and board hedging-policy approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of an International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year; first return due on the next 30 June following incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the annual government fee; persistent failure beyond three months after the due date may lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Licence Fee / Government Annual Renewal Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before 30 June of each calendar year; fee is fixed by reference to authorised capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment attracts a late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee; non-payment for more than three months may result in licence cancellation, removal from the Register, and automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Office, Directors, Members, and Beneficial Ownership Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the Annual Return on or before 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate confirmation exposes the company, directors, and registered agent to statutory fines under the International Companies Act and to AML/CFT penalties if beneficial ownership data is false or withheld.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold triggers an automatic audit for a Samoa International Company. Audit becomes compulsory only when the company conducts a regulated financial activity, when the Registrar or Financial Intelligence Unit directs an examination, or when shareholders holding at least 10% of issued capital request an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Samoa International Companies are tax-exempt and are not required to file audited financial statements. Where financial statements are voluntarily prepared, IFRS or simplified cash-basis records are acceptable; no prescribed local GAAP applies for international companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must annually refresh its customer due-diligence file and confirm the identity and percentage shareholding of each ultimate beneficial owner. Any share transfer or beneficial ownership change during the year is recorded confidentially at the registered office, and the registered agent must update the private UBO record and report to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit as required under Samoa's AML/CFT Regulations. No public UBO registry filing is required.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 1,500 per annum for licensed Samoa registered agent services, inclusive of registered office, registered agent address, and Annual Return preparation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per engagement only if an audit becomes compulsory; otherwise USD 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard corporate income tax rate on Samoa-source income of resident domestic companies; 0% for International Companies on all international business income by statutory exemption.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are effectively tax-exempt on offshore income: 20-year statutory tax holiday (renewable) under s.199 of the International Companies Act 1987, extended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 1998; full exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and withholding tax on distributions to non-residents; no thin capitalization limitation applies to exempt income streams.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Form CIT-1) filed via the Samoa Ministry of Revenue e-Tax portal for any Samoa-source income; International Companies generally file a nil/exempt return only when local-source income is derived.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end balance date (standard balance date 31 December; return due 30 June); self-assessment payment due on the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Samoa-source assessable business income derived during the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: International Company: enter 0 where all receipts derive from offshore cargo charter brokering and no Samoa-source services are performed; attach a schedule categorizing receipts by source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempt under s.199 of the International Companies Act 1987 covering all offshore trading, brokering, and charter-arrangement income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter gross exempt amount with reference to the SIFSA Certificate of Exemption; no supporting tax schedule required, but retain board minutes evidencing offshore management decisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses including charter hire, fuel, brokerage commissions, communications, and registered agent fees allocable to exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claims must not reduce non-exempt taxable income; maintain segmented profit-and-loss accounts consistent with the IC audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa withholding taxes withheld on dividends, interest, or royalties derived by the IC from domestic sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form WHT certificates and reconcile to the IC bank statements; exempt ICs rarely complete this box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 20% of the tax payable (minimum WST 200); late payment interest accrues at 2% per month on unpaid balances; false or misleading returns attract an additional 100% penalty on the shortfall and prosecution of directors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (SIFSA Form AR-IC) filed via the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) online filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 31 days following each anniversary of the date of incorporation, not the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, company number, registered office address in Samoa, and licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the registered agent in Samoa is a SIFSA-licensed Trust Company; any agent change must be endorsed within 14 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, address, nationality, and shareholding percentage of each shareholder; details of directors and secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners may be natural persons or corporate shareholders; the beneficial ownership register must be current and available for inspection under the International Companies beneficial ownership requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C (Statement of No Local Business)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC did not carry on business with Samoa residents or derive Samoa-source income during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A false declaration converting local trading into an IC wrapper invalidates the exemption and triggers retrospective taxation and deregistration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D (Annual Fee and Penalty Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Government annual fee and SIFSA filing acknowledgment for the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annual government fee is generally assessed at WST 1,000 or equivalent USD and must be settled before the return is accepted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fee of WST 100 per month after the anniversary date; persistent default for 6 months exposes the IC to administrative strike-off from the register and forfeiture of assets to the Crown; directors are personally liable for unpaid annual fees and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a resident Samoa company to non-resident shareholders; 0% for International Companies paying dividends to non-resident shareholders by express exemption under s.199 of the International Companies Act 1987.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa comprehensive DTA network is limited; the principal in-force DTA is the Samoa-China Double Taxation Agreement. Protocol: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder home jurisdiction tax authority; (2) submit the TRC, Form WHT-R (Application for Treaty Relief), and supporting dividend documentation to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before payment, or within 12 months of payment for refund; (3) the Ministry issues a direction permitting payment at the reduced rate for a defined period, usually 12 months; (4) retain the approved application for audit evidence. Unilateral relief is not available; absent treaty, the statutory 15% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 15%, royalties 15% on payments to non-residents. Treaty rates under the Samoa-China DTA: dividends 10%, interest 10%, royalties 10%. Intercompany charter-brokerage service fees are not subject to withholding tax but remain subject to transfer pricing adjustment and source-country rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No formal Samoa transfer pricing documentation threshold is legislated for International Companies; however, the Income Tax Act 1974 ss.81-83 authorizes the Commissioner to reallocate international transactions to an arm's length basis. SIFSA expects gross related-party charter and brokerage flows exceeding WST 2,000,000 per annum to be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and functional analysis) aligned to the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply through the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFSA administrative guidance. An International Company must maintain a registered office and licensed registered agent in Samoa and demonstrate effective management in Samoa through board meetings or written resolutions. For an air cargo charter broker, acceptable substance evidence includes: senior management meetings in Samoa, charter contracts signed by Samoa-resident officers, billing and collection routed through Samoa bank accounts, and a commensurate local payroll and office footprint. Failure to maintain substance allows SIFSA to strike off the IC or reclassify it as a Samoa-resident taxable company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Tax-Exempt Status (Domestic Revenue Contamination)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an International Company to broker air cargo charters for Samoa residents, earn freight income sourced within Samoa, or enter into back-to-back contracts that shift Samoa-source profits offshore while claiming the IC tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive withdrawal of the s.199 exemption; back-assessment at the 27% corporate rate for all years involved; a 100% shortfall penalty and 2% monthly late-payment interest; deregistration of the IC under the International Companies Act 1987.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the false exemption claim are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; criminal conviction for tax evasion carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to WST 100,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of related-party charter revenue, fabrication of deductible costs, destruction of books, or submission of false evidence to the Ministry of Revenue or SIFSA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded plus 2% monthly interest; seizure of bank accounts; criminal conviction imposing a fine not exceeding WST 200,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is statutorily permitted: directors and shadow directors are personally liable for restitution of the shortfall where the IC is insolvent; travel bans and asset freezing orders may be issued by the Supreme Court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an International Company with no physical presence, no local management, nominee-only officers, and no evidence of decision-making for charter broker contracts, thereby facilitating tax avoidance or another party's tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFSA strike-off and dissolution; loss of limited liability protection; revocation of the registered agent's license for the IC; inclusion on a publicly listed struck-off register damaging bank and counterparty standing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally sued by creditors if the IC traded with willful disregard for substance requirements; the court may disqualify directors for up to 5 years and issue deportation or travel-ban orders where the director is non-resident.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Swift wire or Fedwire settlements from undisclosed charter principals or shell counterparties without Customer Due Diligence, and processing third-party settlements not mirrored by valid cargo charter agreements, in breach of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory penalties for body corporates up to WST 1,000,000 plus daily default fines; freezing of accounts; suspension or revocation of the air cargo brokerage license; requirement to appoint a SIFSA-approved compliance officer and external auditor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, senior managers, and compliance officers are personally exposed to criminal money laundering charges carrying imprisonment up to 14 years and property forfeiture; travel bans can be imposed pending prosecution, and professional disqualification orders terminate director service.
